## load pharmaceuticals file

```{r}
PH <- read.csv("C:/Users/ptobo/Desktop/Kent State/3 Fundamentals of Machine Learning BA-64060/Assignments/Assignment 4/Pharmaceuticals.csv")

PH

```

## adjusting column numbers to symbol and only use columns 3 through 11


```{r}


rownames(PH) <- PH$Symbol


num_vars <- PH[, 3:11]

num_vars
```

## simplifying scale process relative to above or below 0


```{r}

scaled_vars <- scale(num_vars)

```

## Euclidean Distance_dendrogram reflect measured data points relationships; Claude assist for clarity but inconclusive

```{r}

dist_matrix <- dist(scaled_vars, method = "euclidean")
hc_ward <- hclust(dist_matrix, method = "ward.D2")

plot(hc_ward, main = "Dendrogram of Pharmaceutical Firms (Ward's Method)",
     xlab = "Firm Symbol", ylab = "Euclidean Distance", sub = "", lwd = 2)
rect.hclust(hc_ward, k = 5, border = 2:6)



```

## set seed to 30 and K-means cluster to 5 groups

```{r}
PH$Cluster <- cutree(hc_ward, k = 5)

set.seed(30)
kmeans_res <- kmeans(scaled_vars, centers = 5, nstart = 10)
PH$KMeans_Cluster <- kmeans_res$cluster


```

## Names of 5 clusters

```{r}
cluster_names <- c("1" = "Stable",
                   "2" = "High costs",
                   "3" = "Med Risk",
                   "4" = "Slow growth",
                   "5" = "Storng Return")
PH$Cluster_Name <- cluster_names[as.character(PH$Cluster)]

split(PH$Symbol, PH$Cluster_Name) 

```



## company comparison by average of aggregate variables

```{r}
cluster_profile <- aggregate(num_vars, by = list(Cluster = PH$Cluster), FUN = mean)
cluster_counts <- aggregate(Symbol ~ Cluster, data = PH, FUN = length)
colnames(cluster_counts)[2] <- "Count"

final_profile <- merge(cluster_counts, cluster_profile, by = "Cluster")
print("=== CLUSTER PROFILES (MEANS) ===")
print(round(final_profile, 2))



```


## reflect recommendation, preferred and differences; clusters 1-stable, slow growth 5.38%, hig profit 20.51%, 2-high costs low return ROA, 3-med risk, fast growth 23.60% and good profit 14.13%  4-slow and stead, growth 6.38% AND 7.5% profit 5-strong, fast growth 18.53%, hig profit 19.58%

```{r}

print(table(PH$Cluster, PH$Median_Recommendation))

print(table(PH$Cluster, PH$Location))

print(table(PH$Cluster, PH$Exchange))



```

## patterns suggest cluster 5 'strong return' and cluster 3 'med risk' to have the most equitable investment opportunities.
